items.title: Fine (CFG) - Create Global Choices

use_case: Lending administrators need standard fine classifications so that every lending policy is set up the same way.
Lending administrators need to enable or disable automatic validation of fine rules per lending policy.
The fine calculation logic needs fixed reference values so that it can branch on the selected type.
outcomes: Create the fine global choices in the Lending solution in Example Development.
Deploy the Lending solution to the target example environments for testing.
Deploy the Lending solution to Example Customization for customization.

technical_details.text: t1: Example Development -> Lending -> Global Choices:

children: Description: Classifies how a lending policy charges fines.
Description: Sets how often a flat fine run occurs.
Target environments: Example Test, Example Production.
Target environment for customization: Example Customization.

acceptance_criteria: The global choice Lending Fine Types will exist in the Lending solution in Example Development with the choices Flat, Daily, and Capped.
The global choice Lending Flat Fine Frequency will exist in the Lending solution in Example Development with the choices Monthly and Weekly.
The Lending solution will be deployed to the target example environments for testing.
The Lending solution will be deployed to the Example Customization environment for customization.

items.title: Fine (DEV) - Plugin: Do fine calculation by type

use_case: The lending business needs fines calculated automatically when a fine line is created, so that no administrator computes values by hand.
Each fine type needs its own calculation method, so that flat and daily lending policies produce correct values.
The Book Copy record needs its fine balance kept current, because lending policies and reporting read that value.
outcomes: Create a plug-in that runs when a Lending Fine Line is created.
Select the calculation method from the lending policy configuration.
Update the Book Copy record and the triggering fine line with the calculated values.

children.text: Retrieve from the Lending Policy (ex_lendingfinelog > ex_lendingpolicy):
Retrieve from the Book Copy record:

children: Write no value and exit without error.

children.text: IF "Fine Cap" contains data AND the calculated value is above "Fine Cap":
children: Set the calculated value to "Fine Cap".
Update the Book Copy column "Fine Balance" (ex_finebalance).
Update the triggering Lending Fine Line with the calculated amount.
Dependency: t1 and the helper library in t4.

acceptance_criteria: A plug-in will exist that is registered on the Create message of the Lending Fine Line table in the Post Operation stage, running synchronously.
When the lending policy Fine Type is Flat, the plug-in will call CalculateFineByFlatRate.
When the lending policy Daily Fine Sub-Type is Overdue Days, the plug-in will call CalculateFineByDaysOverdue.
When neither branch matches, the plug-in will exit without writing a value and without raising an error.

When the lending policy "Fine Cap" is 10.00, a calculated fine of 12.50 will be saved as 10.00 and a calculated fine of 7.50 will be saved as 7.50; when "Fine Cap" is empty, the calculated fine will be saved unchanged.
The plug-in will update the "Fine Balance" (ex_finebalance) value on the Book Copy record.
The plug-in will update the calculated amount on the Lending Fine Line that triggered it.
The plug-in assembly will be deployed to the Lending solution in Example Development.

items.title: Fine (INT) - Power Automate: Scheduled fine calculation

use_case: Branch librarians need fines calculated on a schedule, so that flat-fine lending policies are processed without manual work.
Each branch needs the run to follow its own configured scheduling preference.
The fine custom action needs a caller, because nothing else triggers a flat-type run.
outcomes: Create a scheduled Power Automate flow in the Lending solution.
Read the branch scheduling configuration from the Lending Settings record.
Call the fine custom action with the eligible lending policies.

technical_details.text: t5: Create a Power Automate Flow:
children: Trigger: Schedule, daily at 4:00 AM library local time

children.text: Retrieve columns from the Lending Settings record:
IF "Lending Fine Schedule Strategy" == "First of month":
children: IF today is not the first day of the month, escape the flow.

children.text: ELSE IF "Lending Fine Schedule Strategy" == "Day of month":
children: IF today does not match "Lending Fine Day", escape the flow.
Escape the flow, because no other strategy is defined.
Call custom action ex_GenerateLendingFineLogs with the retrieved lending policy identifiers.
On failure, record the run outcome on the Lending Settings record and notify the circulation desk mailbox.
Re-running on the same day creates no duplicate fine log.
Dependency: the custom API in t6.

acceptance_criteria: A Power Automate flow will exist in the Lending solution with a schedule trigger that runs daily at 4:00 AM library local time.
The flow will read the four scheduling columns from the Lending Settings record on every run.
When the schedule strategy is First of month and today is not the first day, the flow will escape without calling the custom action.
When the schedule strategy is Day of month and today does not match the configured day, the flow will escape without calling the custom action.
When the schedule conditions are met, the flow will retrieve every Lending Policy where Fine Type is Flat and fine rules are validated.
The flow will pass the retrieved lending policy identifiers to ex_GenerateLendingFineLogs.
A second run on the same day will create no duplicate fine log.
A failed run will notify the circulation desk mailbox.
